chapter_title: Concerning the Fifteen Paths; and whether the Cate
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation

**¶2:**
For we have received this teaching from you: Fifteen distinct progressions of spiritual life are ordered within the intermediate state between heaven and hell. Four of these progressions are entirely pure and belong [GAP-1] to divine wisdom, leading upward into eternal life. Eight other progressions are [GAP-2] intermingled with good and evil, leading the spirit upward out of that condition. Whatever is of wisdom shall ascend and become liberated through them, be purified, and pass in [GAP-3] to the doctrinal forms that carry truth toward heaven. However, what is refuse — evil and falsity that cannot be assimilated to good — is separated out and cast down into further states of vastation; and the remaining three progressions of [GAP-4] spiritual refuse are discharged into the hells.

**¶3:**
You have explained [GAP-5] that the three progressions belonging to spiritual refuse, those that are drawn toward the hells, originate from the proprium — from what is merely of the natural self-life. The first of them is the lust of the natural will for what is contrary to divine order, which belongs to all people and to every form of the self-life. The second is the [GAP-6] destructive force that inhabits all external forms of the mind, which is the annihilation of charity, [GAP-7] through which every form of self-life is consumed and laid waste. The third is the profaning action, which [GAP-8] assaults the divine truth dispersed throughout creation and every external form of the spirit — together with all remaining falsity and the blasphemy that wounds what is divine.

**¶4:**
These three progressions toward the hells you have taught us. And you have also [GAP-9] taught us that every person follows the course determined by his own spiritual works, whether toward life in heaven or indeed toward spiritual death.

**¶13:**
At once all the prior states of good that a person produced before receiving genuine interior acknowledgment of truth are freed from every condition in which they had been held captive and entangled. Their bondage is loosened and they ascend out of every interior and exterior region of the mind — out of the perceptions and out of the self-life. They are released from every state in which they subsisted and rise toward the celestial heights.

**¶15:**
Now this matter is understood in this manner: it is as when a ruling love dwells within a particular doctrine, while the whole company of its subordinate affections [GAP-10] is present throughout the doctrinal forms, the habitations of thought, and the lesser arrangements [GAP-11] of the mind's domain. So long as the ruling love abides in that state, one finds every power attendant upon it dwelling in those mental habitations that surround it. And whenever the ruling love may [GAP-12] issue the directive for departure from that state of the mind, when it wills [GAP-13] to proceed toward a new condition, an intimation goes forth from it to the whole company of its attendant affections, so that each may set out upon its course and depart [GAP-14] from every state in which it dwells. And each proceeds to the condition appointed for it.

**¶16:**
Thus there are some among the subordinate affections of the ruling love that shall advance before it and arrive prior to it. And there are others among them that shall await it and travel together with it; they depart [GAP-15] at the moment of its own departure. Also, there are others among them that shall come after it, following behind. These continue through [GAP-16] very many successive states and intervals of progression until at last they arrive.

**¶17:**
The entire company of subordinate affections does not depart at a single moment; rather, one proceeds first and another follows after, while still others depart simultaneously with the ruling love.

**¶18:**
There are some among a person's spiritual faculties and works that are purified while he still inhabits the natural body. These are cleansed within [GAP-17] the higher rational planes of the mind and ascend before him. There are also some among his faculties that are freed together with him, at the moment when his spirit separates from the body. And there are others that shall be freed after him from the bonds of the natural world and of creaturely existence. [GAP-18] These proceed onward and reach him in the kingdom of heavenly life.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: For we have heard thus from you: ‘Fifteen paths are drawn out in the zone. Four paths are pure and belong [to the] Light, leading up to life. Eight other paths are [mixed], leading above from that place. The Light shall go [u]p and become free through them; be purified and go in [to the] ships. However, the waste is separated and thrown [dow]n to transmigr[a]tion and the other three paths of [waste are] discharged to the gehennas’.

You have explained [that the three] paths that belong to waste, the ones that are drawn to the gehennas, [a]re drawn from the fleshes. O[n]e of them is the appetite for [lawl]essness, that of people and of all flesh. The second is the [destruction of] all bodies, which is slaughter, [with] which all flesh is consumed. The third is the damaging action, which [harms] the Cross of Light and every body; together with the rest of the error and the blasphemy that wounds the gods.
Th[ese th]ree paths have you taught us, that they lead to the gehennas. And you have also [told] us that every person shall follow after hi[s] de[e]ds, whether to life or indeed to death.

Immediately all his first deeds, that he did before he received the knowledge, shall be freed from every place wherein they are [bou]nd and snared. They shall loosen their bond and asce[n]d from heaven and earth, from the trees and the fleshes. They are loosened from every place wherein they are and go to the heights

Now this matter is like this, the way [som]eone might dwell at a city, while his enti[re] following [is present] in the cities and the dwellings and the villages [of the country]. As long as, overall, the king is living in t[hat] place, you shall find his entire host living in those [dwelli]ngs that surround it. Also, whenever he may [give ... / ...] the sign for departure to the country, when he wishes [to go] to it, an indication is given by him to his entire follow[ing] so that he might set out on the road and depart [from] each [pl]ace wherein it is. And he goes to the place where it i[s].

So, there are some among his expedition who shall travel before him and be prior to him. And there are others am[ong t]hem who shall wait for him and travel with him. They depart [at] his departure. Also, there are others among them who shall come after him, travelling behind him. They continue [very] many days and months travelling until they arrive.
His entire following shall not depart a[t] a single time; but someone shall go first and another after him, while others shall depart with him.

There are some among his limbs and his deeds shall be puri[f]ied while he is set in the body. They are cleansed in [the] firmaments of the heavens and go before him. [Th]ere are some also among his limbs shall be freed wi[t]h him, at the time when he comes out from [h]is body. There are others shall be freed [af]ter him from the bonds of the earth and that of the creatures. [They] go and reach him in the land of the living.

fills.explanation: The spiritual reading confirms these paths "belong to divine wisdom," and in the Kephalaia's natural register the Light is the standard term — "belong to the Light" requires the preposition and article "to the."
The spiritual reading says "intermingled with good and evil," and "mixed" is the standard Manichaean Kephalaia term for the mixture of Light and Darkness in the intermediate zone.
The spiritual reading says "pass in to the doctrinal forms that carry truth toward heaven," corresponding to the ships in the natural register — "go in to the ships" requires "to the."
The spiritual reading says "spiritual refuse are discharged into the hells," and the sentence requires a subject complement and verb: "three paths of waste are discharged to the gehennas."

The spiritual reading confirms "that the three progressions belonging to spiritual refuse," and the following text explicitly names "paths that belong to waste" — requiring "that the three" as the introductory clause.

The spiritual reading identifies this as "the destructive force that inhabits all external forms," and in the Kephalaia's natural register the second evil path — slaughter of bodies — is expressed as the "destruction of all bodies."
The spiritual reading says "through which every form of self-life is consumed," and "with which" is the Kephalaia's standard instrumental construction meaning "by means of which."
The spiritual reading says "assaults the divine truth dispersed throughout creation," and "harms" is the appropriate Kephalaia verb for damaging action directed against the Cross of Light.

The spiritual reading says "taught us," and the editor's "told" is the natural Kephalaia verb for the master communicating doctrine to disciples — both fit, and "told" matches the disciple's voice addressing the teacher.

The spiritual reading confirms the subordinate affections are "present throughout the doctrinal forms," and "is present" is the natural expression for the following being distributed across the cities and dwellings.
The spiritual reading says "of the mind's domain," which in the parable's natural register is "of the country" — the territorial domain over which the king rules.
The spiritual reading says "to proceed toward a new condition," and in the parable's natural register "to go" is the standard verb of movement — "when he wishes to go to it."
The spiritual reading says "from every state in which it dwells," and "depart from each place" requires the preposition "from" to complete the sense of leaving.
The spiritual reading confirms "at the moment of its own departure," and "at his departure" is the natural temporal construction in the Kephalaia.
The spiritual reading confirms "very many successive states and intervals," and "very many days and months" is the natural-plane expression for an extended duration of progressive spiritual travel.
The spiritual reading says "within the higher rational planes of the mind," and "in the firmaments of the heavens" requires the definite article "the" before "firmaments."
The spiritual reading confirms "These proceed onward and reach him," and "They" is the correct pronoun referring back to the others freed after him from the bonds of the earth.
